title: The Evidence from Kenyon's Excavations in Jerusalem: A Response Essay, in Jerusalem in Bible and Archaeology: The First Temple Period
author: Margreet L. Steiner
publisher: Society of Biblical Literature (ed. Andrew G. Vaughn and Ann E. Killebrew), pp. 347-364
allowedUseNotes: Copyrighted edited-volume chapter. Project stores its own summary of the argument only; no reproduction of the chapter's text, plans, or photographs.
summary: A skeptical/minimalist-leaning re-reading of Kathleen Kenyon's own City of David excavation data (Kenyon dug at the site 1961-1967), published in direct dialogue with Cahill's maximalist chapter in the same volume (cahill-2003-jerusalem-united-monarchy). Steiner argues the excavated evidence Kenyon actually recovered supports, at most, a modest, sparsely built 10th-century BCE hill settlement rather than a monumental fortified capital, and cautions against reading later building phases or ambiguous stratigraphy back into the United Monarchy period. This project cites Steiner as the named, checkable minimalist counterpart to Cahill, published in the same edited volume as an explicit scholarly exchange rather than an isolated claim.
